title: Longest increasing subsequence of [10, 9, 2, 5, 3, 7, 101, 18] in O(n log n)

frames.note: tails[k] = the smallest value that can end an increasing run of length k+1. Start with no tails
10 is bigger than every tail: append it, length 1
9 replaces 10 at tails[0]: a run of length 1 can now end lower, at 9
2 replaces 9 at tails[0]: a run of length 1 can now end lower, at 2
5 is bigger than every tail: append it, length 2
3 replaces 5 at tails[1]: a run of length 2 can now end lower, at 3
7 is bigger than every tail: append it, length 3
101 is bigger than every tail: append it, length 4
18 replaces 101 at tails[3]: a run of length 4 can now end lower, at 18
Longest increasing subsequence has length 4, for example [2, 3, 7, 18] (tails itself is not always a real subsequence)
